questions.q: When presenting findings to a busy stakeholder, what should come first?
options: A step-by-step account of every cleaning step
A list of every library you used
A one-sentence headline that answers their question, followed by the evidence
questions.explain: Lead with the answer, then support it with evidence, the action it suggests, caveats, and next steps.

questions.q: Why are caveats such as "the top discount band has only 103 orders" worth including?
options: They make the analysis more credible by being honest about what could make you wrong
They are only needed for machine learning projects
questions.explain: Clear limits build trust and prevent overstating an association as proof.

questions.q: Why compute report numbers with code (for example, a summary dictionary) instead of typing them in?
options: Typing numbers is not allowed in Markdown
So the figures are reproducible and cannot drift from the data when the pipeline is rerun
questions.explain: Numbers generated from the cleaned data always match the analysis, and rerunning the pipeline updates them automatically.

questions.q: Which item does NOT belong in a public portfolio repository?
options: API keys, passwords, or private customer data
questions.explain: Never publish secrets or private data. Requirements, a README, and tests all make a project stronger.

questions.q: What does the next course in the Data Scientist path, Statistics & Probability for Data Science, add to this capstone?
options: How to judge how confident you can be in a difference or an association, such as 7% versus 13% return rates
questions.explain: Statistics gives you the tools to quantify uncertainty and decide when an observed difference deserves to be called a finding.
